q: What happens to my Senseible records if my paid plan expires or I cancel?
title: When a Senseible plan expires
short: Your records stay. When a paid Senseible plan ends, it stays in force for 7 more days so you can renew. After that the account moves to the free Snapshot plan: your invoices, emission records and reports remain saved on the server, and only the paid allowances stop.
audience: Paying Senseible users and prospects checking for lock-in

sections.h: The 7 days after the paid period ends
p: The plan you paid for, Essential or Pro, keeps working for 7 days after its paid period ends. This covers a renewal paid a few days late. During those days the account is told when access will change.

ul: The account falls back to Snapshot, the free plan.
New invoice reads drop to Snapshot's allowance of 10 a month.
The paid plan's allowances stop, and Snapshot's features apply until you renew.
Nothing you already uploaded is deleted because the plan lapsed: documents, emission lines, verification status and earlier reports are kept.

p: Extra Invoice Scans (₹79 per 100 scans, before GST, bought on your Subscription page) keep their own validity: 12 months when bought on a yearly plan, 30 days otherwise. A lapsed plan does not cancel scans that are still valid. Fast-track Verification and the Expert Climate Audit are paid per report or once, not tied to the subscription.

Pay for a plan again from the pricing page and its allowances come back on the same account, with your history in place. There is no re-upload and no new account. Keeping that history matters: the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard expects you to compare each year against a base year you can recalculate from the original records.
Refund terms for cancelled subscriptions are set out in the Refund and Cancellation Policy.

senseible: This page describes how Senseible plans behave: a 7-day period after a paid plan ends, then the free Snapshot plan, with your records kept on the server. For a specific billing question, write to the Senseible team.
